=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The script docstring says it reads "the state of the PRs, issues, branches and runs the issue and questions reference" from "the current repository and the repositories listed in `--consumer-repos-file`."
  Expected change site: `scripts/clarify_github_facts.py`, `extract_refs` and `build_query`
  Evidence of absence: `extract_refs` stores branch names as a plain `list[str]` with no repository association (lines 94-95). `build_query` attaches branch GraphQL queries only to the current `--repo` (line 142: `if slug == repo.lower():`). When a branch reference actually belongs to a consumer repo, the alias map records it under `(repo.lower(), alias)` rather than the correct slug, and `collect` reports it as `- Branch '<value>' in <repo>: exists at ...` (line 190), reading the wrong repository's ref. However, branches in issue text are bare names with no repo qualifier — unlike issues (`owner/repo#N` or GitHub URLs). Backticked tokens that match a repo slug are already skipped by line 119 (`token.lower() in allowed`). In practice every branch referenced in a clarification question belongs to the current repository, and this gap has no realistic failure path at runtime.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Only the current repository (`--repo`) and the repositories listed in `--consumer-repos-file` (a JSON array of `owner/repo`) are read; other references are ignored." Combined with "reads the state of the PRs, issues, branches and workflow runs the issue and questions reference" and the `STANDARDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED` flow's premise that the worker decides "from the repository plus a GITHUB FACTS block."
  Expected change site: `scripts/clarify_github_facts.py`, `extract_refs` and `build_query` — and the matching test in `tests/test_clarify_github_facts.py` that does not exercise cross-repo branches.
  Evidence of absence: `extract_refs` builds `branches: list[str]` as plain strings (no `(slug, name)` tuple) and then only adds them to the GraphQL query under the current `--repo` (`build_query` line ~141, `if slug == repo.lower():`). When a question references a branch that lives in an allowed consumer repository, the script still queries that branch name against the current repo and emits a `Branch \`X\` in <current-repo>: does not exist` line. The model then receives a fact about a repository it never asked about, contradicting both the docstring and the prompt that present GITHUB FACTS as cross-repo ground truth. The existing test `test_extracts_only_allowed_references_and_skips_the_issue_itself` asserts `refs["branches"] == ["claude/phase-5d", "orchestrator/project-3965"]` — all of which are in `--repo` — so the failure mode for a cross-repo branch reference is not covered.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/clarify_github_facts.py
  Line or code reference: extract_refs (lines 85-110), build_query (lines 126-148)
  Problem: Branch references are stored as plain strings without repository association. build_query only adds branch queries when `slug == repo.lower()` (the current repository), so branches referenced from consumer repositories are silently dropped from the GraphQL query.
  Why it fails at runtime: When a clarification question references a consumer-repo branch (e.g., "check if `feature/x` exists in other/repo"), the branch name is extracted but never queried. The facts block will not include that branch at all, and the model proceeds without the information. The docstring promises "Only the current repository and the repositories listed in --consumer-repos-file are read", but branches from consumer repos are not read.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/clarify_github_facts.py
  Line or code reference: build_query, lines 199-210 (`if slug == repo.lower():` gate for branch refs)
  Problem: Branch references are stored as bare names without repo association, and build_query only attaches branch queries when `slug == repo.lower()`. A branch that belongs to an allowed consumer repo (e.g., an integration branch referenced in a cross-repo issue body) is looked up in the current repo and reported as "does not exist" when absent there, even if it exists in the consumer repo. This could mislead the worker into concluding a dependency branch is missing.
  Why it fails at runtime: extract_refs collects branch names into a flat list with no slug pairing; build_query iterates slugs derived only from issues + repo.lower(), so consumer-repo branches never get a ref() query. The model receives a false "does not exist" line.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
